subject: Maths
title: Maths Exam 11
intro: Edexcel Higher style. No calculator. Show your working in the working box: method marks count even if the final answer slips. Before you divide, ask: is the number I'm dividing by bigger or smaller than 1? With prime factors, check what happens to every power.

questions.q: Without working them out, which calculation gives an answer bigger than 36?
questions.ms: 36 ÷ 0.8 = 45. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the answer bigger. The others are 28.8, 30 and 34.2, all smaller than 36.

questions.q: Work out 2.4 ÷ 0.06
questions.ms: 40. Multiply both numbers by 100: 240 ÷ 6 = 40. (How many 0.06s fit into 2.4? Lots more than 2.4.)

questions.q: Work out an estimate for the value of 21.3 × 5.920.208
questions.ms: 600. M1 round each number to 1 s.f.: 20, 6, 0.2. M1 20 × 6 = 120. A1 120 ÷ 0.2 = 600 (dividing by 0.2 is the same as multiplying by 5).

questions.q:
Omar works out 63 ÷ 0.7 and gets the answer 9.
Explain why Omar's answer must be wrong, and work out the correct answer.
questions.ms: B1 0.7 is less than 1, so the answer must be bigger than 63 (Omar's answer is smaller). B1 90 (630 ÷ 7 = 90).

questions.q:
You are given that 238 × 56 = 13 328.
Work out 23.8 × 5.6
questions.ms: 133.28. One decimal place in each number, so two in the answer: 13 328 ÷ 100.
2380. 13 328 ÷ 56 = 238, and 5.6 is 10 times smaller than 56, so the answer is 10 times bigger.
5600. 1332.8 is 10 times smaller than 13 328, and 0.238 is 1000 times smaller than 238, so the answer is 56 × 1000 ÷ 10 = 5600.
56. Both numbers are 100 times smaller than in 13 328 ÷ 238, so the answer stays 56.

questions.q: Work out (−3)<sup>2</sup> − 4 × (−2)<sup>3</sup>
Work out −3 − (−4)<sup>2</sup> ÷ 8
questions.ms: −5. M1 (−4)² = 16 and 16 ÷ 8 = 2 (powers, then divide, then subtract), A1 −3 − 2 = −5. The minus in front of the bracket is not squared.

questions.q: Round 0.003 0049 to 3 significant figures.
questions.ms: 0.00300. The first significant figure is the 3; the next two are 0 and 0, and the 4 after them means round down. The zeros must stay to show 3 s.f.

questions.q: Write 540 as a product of its prime factors. Give your answer in index form.
questions.ms: 2² × 3³ × 5. M1 a correct factor tree or repeated division, A1 index form.

questions.q: Write 540<sup>2</sup> as a product of its prime factors in index form.
questions.ms: 2⁴ × 3⁶ × 5². Squaring multiplies every power by 2: (2² × 3³ × 5¹)². 5 is 5¹, so it becomes 5². B1 for two powers correct.

questions.q:
B = 23 × 32 × 7
Write B3 as a product of its prime factors in index form.
questions.ms: 2⁹ × 3⁶ × 7³. Cubing multiplies every power by 3: 3 × 3 = 9, 2 × 3 = 6, 1 × 3 = 3. B1 for two powers correct.

questions.q:
C = 26 × 54
Write √C as a product of its prime factors in index form.
questions.ms: 2³ × 5². A square root halves every power: 6 ÷ 2 = 3, 4 ÷ 2 = 2 (check: 2³ × 5² = 200 and 200² = 40 000 = C). B1 for one power correct.

questions.q: Use your answer to question 9 to explain why 540 is not a square number.
questions.ms: B1 in 2² × 3³ × 5 the powers of 3 and 5 (3 and 1) are odd; a square number has every power even.

questions.q: Find the smallest whole number you can multiply 540 by to make a square number.

84 = 22 × 3 × 7 and 90 = 2 × 32 × 5
Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 90.
questions.ms: 6. M1 primes in both, lowest powers: 2 × 3, A1 6.

questions.q:
Yassin runs one lap of a track every 84 seconds. Sami runs one lap every 90 seconds. They start together at the start line.
After how many minutes will they next be at the start line together?
questions.ms: 21 minutes. M1 recognises the LCM is needed, M1 2² × 3² × 5 × 7 = 1260 seconds (every prime, highest power), A1 1260 ÷ 60 = 21 minutes. Check the multiplication: 4 × 9 = 36, 36 × 35 = 1260.

questions.q: Which of these numbers is the largest?
questions.ms: 4.1 × 10⁻³. Write them all as ordinary decimals: 0.0039, 0.00395, 0.00405, 0.0041.

questions.q: Work out (8 × 10<sup>−3</sup>) × (4 × 10<sup>7</sup>). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.ms: 3.2 × 10⁵. M1 8 × 4 = 32 and 10⁻³ × 10⁷ = 10⁴, so 32 × 10⁴, A1 3.2 × 10⁵ (32 is not between 1 and 10, so adjust).

questions.q: Work out (7.2 × 10<sup>6</sup>) ÷ (9 × 10<sup>−2</sup>). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.ms: 8 × 10⁷. M1 7.2 ÷ 9 = 0.8 and 10⁶ ÷ 10⁻² = 10⁸, so 0.8 × 10⁸, A1 8 × 10⁷ (0.8 is less than 1, so adjust).

questions.q: Find the value of x when 8x = 210 × 4
questions.ms: x = 4. M1 8 = 2³ so 8ˣ = 2³ˣ, and 2¹⁰ × 4 = 2¹⁰ × 2² = 2¹², M1 3x = 12, A1 x = 4. Give the value of x, not 2¹².

questions.q: Solve 27n ÷ 3 = 94
questions.ms: n = 3. M1 write everything as powers of 3: 27ⁿ = 3³ⁿ and 9⁴ = 3⁸, M1 3³ⁿ ÷ 3¹ = 3³ⁿ⁻¹ so 3n − 1 = 8, A1 n = 3.

questions.q: Simplify fully √98 − √18
questions.ms: 4√2. M1 √98 = √49 × √2 = 7√2 and √18 = √9 × √2 = 3√2, A1 7√2 − 3√2 = 4√2. You can't subtract under the root: it is not √80.

questions.q:
A rectangle has length √72 cm and width √18 cm.
Show that the area of the rectangle is a whole number of cm², and give the area.
Work out the perimeter of the rectangle. Give your answer in the form a√2
questions.ms: 18√2 cm. M1 √72 = √36 × √2 = 6√2 and √18 = √9 × √2 = 3√2, M1 2 × (6√2 + 3√2), A1 18√2. Simplify each surd first; don't add under the root.
